title: Multiplicity one in a simple Weil sheaf with semisimple geometric carrier
statement: Let $k_0$ be a finite field, $\ell$ a prime different from its characteristic, and $X/k_0$ a finite-type scheme with irreducible geometric fiber $\bar X$. Let $V$ be an irreducible lisse Weil sheaf [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. For any finite decomposition $\bar V\simeq\bigoplus_{a<N}T_a$ into irreducible geometric local systems, the factors are pairwise nonisomorphic: if $T_a\simeq T_b$, then $a=b$. This asserts only multiplicity one in the given decomposition, and no Frobenius-periodic structures or transports.

source.place: Paragraphs 1--2: the Frobenius orbit of geometric isotypic blocks and the multiplicity eigenline; applied to a simple Weil object.

proof.text: Choose an embedded simple factor S of the given nonzero carrier. Every Frobenius translate embeds and has a nonzero projection to one of the finitely many given simple factors; Schur identifies the two. Pigeonhole gives two isomorphic translates. Cancel the smaller Frobenius power and choose the least positive period d. Its first d translates are pairwise nonisomorphic. The helpers q_irreducible, period_of_pair, and exists_least_period implement this argument.

Apply exists_simple_frobenius_eigenembedding to S, its embedding, and the isomorphism from its d-th Frobenius pullback. This gives a new embedding j and an isomorphism e such that e followed by j equals the d-th translate of j.

The direct sum of the first d translates of j is mono: a nonzero lisse kernel would contain a simple local system, and its nonzero projection to one translate is an isomorphism. All other projections vanish by pairwise nonisomorphism, contradicting the injectivity of that translate. The cyclic return on this sum is mono by compatibility with the embedding and is invertible by equality of stalk ranks. It defines a nonzero lisse Weil subobject; arithmetic irreducibility makes its embedding an isomorphism.

Compare the given decomposition with this multiplicity-free decomposition. A simple summand has a nonzero projection to some new summand, which is an isomorphism; all other projections vanish. For two isomorphic original factors both embeddings therefore factor through that one new summand. Composing with the original biproduct projections forces the identity of one nonzero factor to vanish unless their indices are equal. The helper distinct_of_iso_biproduct formalizes this comparison.

proof_origin.place: Paragraphs 1--2; Hom-space eigenvector version of the multiplicity-eigenline argument. Finite-period, cyclic-sum and decomposition-comparison glue proved explicitly in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem geometric_factors_pairwise_nonisomorphic
    {k₀ : Type u} [Field k₀] [Finite k₀] {l : ℕ} [Fact l.Prime]
    [Fact (ringChar k₀ ≠ l)] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [IrreducibleSpace (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)).geometricFiber]
    (V : WeilSheaf k₀ l X) (hV : V.IsIrreducibleLisse)
    (N : ℕ) (T : Fin N → AdicSheaf l (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)).geometricFiber)
    (hT : ∀ i, IsIrreducibleAdicLocalSystem (T i)) (vT : V.obj.carrier ≅ ⨁ T) :
    ∀ a b, Nonempty (T a ≅ T b) → a = b
